standard_prerequisites.name: Pushout of a span
standard_prerequisites.statement: The pushout A \sqcup^C B is the higher inductive type generated by \inl : A \to A\sqcup^C B, \inr : B \to A\sqcup^C B and \glue : \prd{x:C} \inl(f(x)) = \inr(g(x)).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose maps the theorem characterises (source lines 953-956).

standard_prerequisites.name: Cocone over the diagram
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cocone consists of maps i : A \to E and j : B \to E together with a homotopy h : \prd{x:C} i(f(x)) = j(g(x)).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the right-hand side of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverse criterion for an equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function is an equivalence as soon as it has a two-sided inverse.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof constructs the inverse s and checks both composites (source lines 1006-1008).

core_obligations: Define the canonical map sending a map t to the cocone (t \circ \inl, t \circ \inr, ap(t) \circ \glue) out of the pushout (source lines 959-963).

For a cocone (i,j,h), construct the map s(c) out of A \sqcup^C B by the induction principle of the pushout, setting s(c)(\inl(a)) \defeq i(a), s(c)(\inr(b)) \defeq j(b) and ap(s(c))(\glue(x)) \defid h(x) (source lines 966-980).
Prove the composite c \mapsto s(c) \mapsto c is the identity, computing the three components of the cocone and using function extensionality on the homotopy component (source lines 982-995).
Prove the other composite is the identity by evaluating s(c_\sqcup(t)) at \inl(a), \inr(b) and \glue(x) (source lines 997-1008).

proof_roadmap.step: Write the canonical map from maps out of the pushout to cocones.
Build the inverse by pushout induction, defining its action on the glue constructor.
Check the second composite on the three constructors and conclude the quasi-inverse.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 953-957 (book Theorem 6.8.2): for every type E, the type of maps A \sqcup^C B \to E is equivalent to the type of cocones over the spanning diagram. The statement gives only the equivalence and neither of its two directions, while the proof (source lines 958-1009) must construct both: the canonical map into cocones, and then a map s(c) out of the pushout for an arbitrary cocone, which is defined by the induction principle and therefore needs its value on the path constructor \glue to be specified as the homotopy h of the cocone. The two composites are then computed by hand, the first through the three components of a cocone together with function extensionality, the second by evaluating the induced map at \inl(a), \inr(b) and \glue(x). Nothing beyond the induction principle is available to produce s(c), so the construction cannot be read off the statement.
